1. SUITE GATE. A class / object whose extends / with clause (tree-sitter `extends_clause`) names a SCALA_TEST_BASES type by its last segment. Only such bodies are scanned, so `"a" in b` in production code is never a case.
2. REGISTRATIONS (tree-sitter shapes over the body's statements). LEAVES: an `infix_expression` whose operator is `in` (or `ignore` / `taggedAs ... in`) and whose right operand is a block - its left operand is the description chain (`"X" should "y"`, `it should "y"`, `they must "y"`, `"y"`), named by joining its string contents and verbs (`OrderService should sum`; `it` is replaced by the enclosing container's subject when there is one); a `call_expression` `test("n")`, `it("n")`, `property("n")`, `scenario("n")`, `Scenario("n")` followed by a block argument or a trailing block. CONTAINERS: infix `"X" should|must|can|when|which { .. }`, `"X" - { .. }`, and calls `describe("X") { .. }` / `Feature("X") { .. }`: their block's statements are visited with the container's text as a prefix (`X should y`). Descriptions are whitespace-collapsed, at most 120 chars, `::` replaced by `:`; a repeated description in one class gets ` #2`, ` #3` (ScalaTest rejects duplicates, but a nested prefix can collide).
3. NODES. emit_test_case: FUNCTION `<class qname>::<description>` (name = description), Confidence::Strong, entity_cells of the registration (CODE, POSITION, DOC), DEFINES from the class, nav parent the class; then collect_calls_in(block, src, id, true, acc) - in_type true, so a bare call to a helper def of the suite is a SelfMethod as in visit_method. The CL.5b pass then treats each case as a ROOT (no function of its module calls it) and mints `TESTS <case> -> <callee>` for every call into the tested module; the grader's `from: OrderServiceSpec` matches the case's qname by substring.

packets.implementation:
1. sbt_subprojects: comments stripped (`//` lines, `/* */` blocks; strings respected). Accepted forms, each bound to a `val` / `lazy val` id: `(project in file("d"))`, `project.in(file("d"))`, `Project("name", file("d"))` / `Project(id = .., base = file("d"))` (sbt 0.13), and a bare `= project` / `= (project)` with optional settings chained after it (dir = the id, sbt's default base). `file(".")` or an empty dir is the root itself and is skipped; a dir with `..`, an absolute path or `${` is rejected; `./x` and a trailing `/` are normalised. Label = the val id through clean_label.
2. walk_dir. The root build.sbt's rel path is the manifest; a member's rel_path = <dir rel>/<d> ('' root joins as d). Members are pushed in declaration order right after the root (roots stay in walk order for every other ecosystem). A member whose directory is absent or collapsed (gitignored, a REGION) is skipped and counted. A sub-directory with its own manifest (an sbt member that does carry a build.sbt, or a package.json inside it) replaces the member entry when the walk reaches it, so a manifest always wins over a declaration, and no rel_path is ever duplicated (the fixture's forbid `project:api` max 1).

packets.title: Rust trait impls across files: `impl Trait for Type` with an imported or path-qualified trait becomes IMPLEMENTS, bound by Rust path rules (RustIndex::resolve_type_refs), never by bare name
packets.area: DG matrix rest A: Rust trait impls (rust/impl)
packets.rationale:
Re-graded at HEAD 84e2e71, glia_py 0.5.1 wheel in ~/.venvs/glia-leap: rust/impl PARTIAL (extract=2/2 literal=2/2 route=0/1). matrix/rust/impl has `pub trait Repo` in repo.rs and `use crate::repo::Repo; impl Repo for SqlRepo` in sql_repo.rs; the dump holds 4 edges, DEFINES / IMPORTS only (IMPORTS sql_repo -> repo). parsers/code/rust/src/lib.rs visit_impl (G12.5) emits IMPLEMENTS only `when the trait is in-file; skip external traits rather than fabricate a target` - so every impl of a trait declared in another file of the crate is dropped, the common case (trait in mod.rs / a traits module, impls beside each type). glia's own graph shows it: repo-graph `impact graph::src::resolvers::mod::CrossGraphResolver direction=backward depth=1` (re-run by the verifier) returns only 3 DOCUMENTS doc sections and marks the trait dead (⊘) - none of the `impl CrossGraphResolver for <X>Resolver` blocks in graph/src/resolvers/*.rs reaches it. A debug-CLI probe of this packet's precision fixture (probe/DG/verify/rtip: a Cargo crate, `use crate::repo::Repo; use std::fmt::Display; impl Repo for SqlRepo; impl Display for SqlRepo` beside a crate-local `pub trait Display`) gives no IMPLEMENTS at all at HEAD.
Binding must follow Rust paths, not names: graph/src/build.rs build_rust runs the generic resolve_refs, whose IMPLEMENTS fallback is a unique repo-wide name - so `use std::fmt::Display; impl Display for SqlRepo` beside the crate's own `trait Display` would bind to the wrong trait. RustIndex (graph/src/rust_paths.rs) already resolves Rust paths for calls and enum variants (LA.1a / LA.1b / LA.3: resolve_variant walks a path from the caller's scope; resolve_leftover_refs binds variant USES).
Scope note (verified): the Rust parser mints no METHOD under a trait (visit_type makes a trait_item an INTERFACE with no member nodes; the matrix dump has no repo::Repo::get), so emit_method_level_implements derives nothing from these edges for Rust - the new edges are type-level only.
entry_points: parsers/code/rust/src/lib.rs - visit_impl - when the `trait` field's base name is not in type_ids AND the impl's self type is an in-file type (type_ids holds base_name, so parent_id is that type, not the scope): push UnresolvedRef { from: parent_id, from_module: acc.file_module, qualifier: Bare(name) for a plain type_identifier / Attribute { base: <path>, name } for a scoped_type_identifier (generic arguments stripped), category: IMPLEMENTS, line: the trait node's 0-based row }; HEAD's in-file IMPLEMENTS edge is unchanged

graph/src/rust_paths.rs - new pub(crate) const TYPE_REF_CATEGORIES: &[(EdgeCategoryId, &[NodeKindId], &str)] = &[(IMPLEMENTS, &[INTERFACE], "trait_impl")] (category, wanted kinds, EVIDENCE rule); new RustIndex::resolve_type_refs(&self, g, refs, rb) and private resolve_type(g, rb, from, qualifier, want) modelled on resolve_variant (start / walk / settle_type_name); RustBindings gains `declared: HashMap<NodeId, HashSet<String>>` (every `use` leaf's bound name per scope, resolved or not), filled in resolve_imports_rust; new RustIndex::report_types (`[rust-types]` marker)

graph/src/build.rs - build_rust - partition all_refs: a ref whose category is in rust_paths::TYPE_REF_CATEGORIES goes to `idx.resolve_type_refs(&mut g, &type_refs, &bindings)` BEFORE resolve_refs; every other ref keeps HEAD's path
parsers/code/rust/src/lib.rs mod tests, graph/src/rust_paths.rs mod tests - new tests; engine/tests/rust_crate_paths.rs - new test trait_impl_across_files
bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/rust-trait-impl-precision/ (new) - key.json, Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/repo.rs, src/display.rs, src/sql.rs
packets.implementation:
1. PARSER. visit_impl keeps HEAD's in-file IMPLEMENTS edge and adds the ref only for a trait not in type_ids; an impl for a type declared elsewhere (`impl Trait for other::Foo`, parent_id falls back to the scope), a blanket `impl<T: X> Tr for T` and `impl Tr for &Foo` emit nothing (no in-file self type to stand on). One ref per impl block.
2. GRAPH. TYPE_REF_CATEGORIES is the one table of Rust type refs this resolver owns (DG.13b adds the INJECTS row; build.rs reads the table, so it is not edited again). resolve_type_refs, per ref in input order: S = the ref's scope (`enclosing(&g.nav, from, true)`: an inline mod or the file MODULE). Bare(name): (a) the scope's `use` binding (rb's module_import_bindings view / fn_scoped) -> its target when that target's kind is wanted; (b) else, when rb.declared lists `name` for S (an external `use` that bound nothing: `use std::fmt::Display;`), the ref is EXTERNAL and dropped - never a fallback; (c) else a type item named `name` declared in S (an inline mod's own trait); (d) else the scope's globs (rb.globs) in their sorted order; (e) else, only in a file whose crate is unknown (loose `.rs` files, resolve_imports_rust's tail_fallback rule - matrix/rust/impl has no Cargo.toml), a unique type of the wanted kinds across the repo. Attribute{base, name}: split_path(base) walked like resolve_variant (`crate::` / `self::` / `super::` / a workspace crate / a `use`-bound module) to a scope, then the type item `name` in it; a first segment bound to an external crate -> dropped. A hit pushes the edge through push_edge with rust_ev(<the row's rule>).line(r.line) (EVIDENCE emitter graph:rust_paths, rule trait_impl); a miss goes back to g.unresolved_refs. The generic resolve_refs never sees these refs, so its name-based fallback cannot bind them.
3. NO METHOD LEVEL. emit_method_level_implements still runs after, but Rust traits carry no METHOD nodes, so it adds nothing for these edges; the packet does not claim method-level IMPLEMENTS (recorded as a gap).
4. MARKER, once per build_rust with any type ref: `[rust-types] implements=<bound>/<refs> injects=<bound>/<refs> external=<e> unbound=<u>` (injects counts 0/0 until DG.13b adds its row).
5. TESTS (parser): trait_impl_of_an_imported_trait_emits_a_ref (Bare and `impl crate::repo::Repo for X` -> Attribute{crate::repo, Repo}; in-file trait keeps the direct edge and pushes no ref; impl for a foreign self type -> nothing). packets.title: Ruby broker rows: Bunny (declared queue + subscribe, default-exchange publish), Karafka routing `topic :x`, google-cloud-pubsub topic / subscription (v2 and v3 spellings), aws-sdk-sqs / aws-sdk-sns snake_case keys; two new topic rules (Declared, BareArg)
packets.area: DH matrix ruby messaging (ruby/amqp, ruby/kafka, ruby/pubsub, ruby/sqs_sns)
packets.rationale: Four Ruby messaging cells read none at HEAD 84e2e71 (0.5.1 wheel, `matrix.py --cell`): ruby/amqp = none via=None extract 0/2 literal 0/2 route 0/1 forbid 0/0; ruby/kafka = none via=queue extract 1/2 literal 1/2 route 0/1 forbid 0/0 reason extract partial: 1/2 expected kinds present; `none` is the all-of rule, not silence; ruby/pubsub = none via=None extract 0/2 literal 0/2 route 0/1 forbid 0/0; ruby/sqs_sns = none via=None extract 0/2 literal 0/2 route 0/1 forbid 0/0. Measured causes (GLIA_QUEUE_DEBUG=1 debug CLI on copies under the probe dir): (1) ruby/amqp - Bunny (https://github.com/ruby-amqp/bunny, the dominant Ruby AMQP client; guide rubybunny.info/articles/queues.html): `q = ch.queue("orders", durable: true)` + `q.subscribe(block: true) { |_, _, body| }` and `ch.default_exchange.publish("order-1", routing_key: "orders")`: no row reads either side (the RabbitMQ rows are amqplib / pika / RabbitMQ.Client / streadway spellings), so no QUEUE_* node at all. (2) ruby/kafka - the WaterDrop producer fires (`[queues] needle '.produce_async(' framework=Kafka gate=ok topic=orders`), the Karafka routing DSL consumer `routes.draw do topic :orders do consumer OrdersConsumer end end` (karafka.io/docs/Routing) has no row; it is a paren-less call with a symbol argument, which no TopicRule reads (ArgLiteral needs a bracket, Keyed needs a key). (3) ruby/pubsub - google-cloud-pubsub (cloud.google.com/ruby/docs/reference/google-cloud-pubsub) `pubsub.topic("orders").publish` / `pubsub.subscription("orders").listen`: the `.topic(` / `.subscription(` rows are gated on the JS package `@google-cloud/pubsub`. (4) ruby/sqs_sns - aws-sdk-sqs `sqs.send_message(queue_url: url)` / `receive_message(queue_url: url)`: the `.send_message(` / `.receive_message(` rows are gated on boto3 / botocore and read the key `queueurl`, which the snake_case Ruby keyword `queue_url` never spells. Every fix keys on the library's real API; none is applicable-in-doubt (Ruby has first-class clients for all four brokers).

parsers/code/extractors/src/queues.rs - emit_queue_nodes - a `TopicRule::BareArg` hit that read no literal is no site (`hits.retain(|h| h.topic.is_some())`, the CL.4 LambdaCallee precedent); a `TopicRule::Declared` hit is an unnamed site with no expression, so bind_declared_queues binds it and an unbound one keeps HEAD's deferred framework tag; the LA.4 `folds` filter excludes both rules

parsers/code/extractors/src/queue_topic.rs - TopicRule - new variants `Declared` (the call names no queue: the file's one declared queue is its identity) and `BareArg` (the first argument of a call written with or without parentheses: a quoted literal or a Ruby / Elixir `:symbol`)

parsers/code/extractors/src/queue_topic.rs - scan_guarded / topic_at / expr_at - `Declared` reads no topic and no expression; `BareArg` skips spaces and tabs after the needle, reads arg_literal(region, 0) when a `(` opens, else read_literal at that byte; never an expression

parsers/code/extractors/src/queue_topic.rs - bare_word_ok - `TopicRule::BareArg` joins `TopicRule::Receiver` in the word-edge test (the needle `topic ` starts with an identifier byte), so an occurrence inside a longer identifier (`subtopic :x`, `my_topic "y"`) is no site; the after-edge test already passes a quote or `:`
packets.implementation: 1. RULES (queue_topic.rs). `TopicRule::Declared`: scan_guarded maps it to (topic None, expr None) for every occurrence - the hit exists only so CL.1's declare pass can bind it. `TopicRule::BareArg`: `bare_arg(source, after)` = skip ` `/`\t`; if the next byte is `(` -> `arg_literal(arg_region(..)?, 0)`; else `read_literal(source, j)` (already reads `'x'`, `"x"` and `:x`). expr_at returns None for both (a Karafka `topic Topics::ORDERS` is not folded: the LA.4 fold needs an expression slot this rule does not define). 2. EMIT (queues.rs emit_queue_nodes): next to the CL.4 LambdaCallee retain, `if matches!(rule, TopicRule::BareArg) { hits.retain(|h| h.topic.is_some()) }` so a prose `# topic name` line in a Karafka file is no site and mints no `unresolved:kafka` tag; the `folds` filter gains `&& !matches!(rule, TopicRule::Declared | TopicRule::BareArg)`. 3. ROWS as listed in entry_points, in one commented block per table placed before the A2.9 block (so the generic `.subscribe(` / `.publish(` RedisPubSub / MQTT rows, which yield to claimed spans, never double-read a Bunny call). Gates are lowercase (signal_lists_are_lowercase). The Bunny gate is the client's construction / require, not the bare word, so a Ruby file mentioning a `bunny` variable stays out. The SQS / SNS gates are the gem names and the `Aws::SQS` / `Aws::SNS` namespaces lowercased. 4. BINDING: the Bunny consumer is CL.1's shape exactly - one `.queue("orders")` declaration + one unnamed `.subscribe(` -> one `queue_consumer:orders` at the subscribe's offset; two declared queues bind nothing and keep HEAD's tag (`declare-unbound`). The default-exchange producer reads `routing_key:` (Bunny's publish option, the queue name on the default exchange); a topic exchange's routing key is read the same way. 5. DERIVED GATES: eventbus.rs's broker gate is derived from these signals (broker_signal_present), so an `ActiveSupport::Notifications.subscribe` in a file that ALSO constructs Bunny is skipped there - intended (A2.9). 6. TESTS (queues.rs mod tests): ruby_bunny_declared_queue_binds_subscribe (matrix/ruby/amqp's worker.rb -> exactly [queue_consumer:orders]); ruby_bunny_two_declared_queues_bind_nothing; ruby_bunny_default_exchange_routing_key (publisher.rb -> [queue_producer:orders]); karafka_topic_symbol_and_string (`topic :orders do` and `topic "orders" do` -> [queue_consumer:orders]); karafka_prose_topic_word_mints_nothing (`# topic name here` in a karafka file -> no node, no tag); ruby_gcp_pubsub_v2_and_v3 (`.topic`/`.subscription` and `.publisher`/`.subscriber`); ruby_aws_sqs_queue_url_folds (send_message / receive_message with an https queue URL -> orders, `[queues] cloud broker=Sqs topic=orders from=url`); ruby_aws_sns_topic_arn_folds; bunny_gate_keeps_other_subscribe_out (`obs.subscribe(` in a Ruby file without Bunny -> nothing). queue_topic.rs mod tests: bare_arg_reads_symbol_string_and_paren_forms; bare_arg_identifier_reads_nothing; declared_reads_no_topic_and_no_expr. 7. WORD EDGE (verifier): scan_guarded's bare_word_ok gates only Receiver at HEAD, and `str::match_indices("topic ")` also hits `subtopic ` / `my_topic ` in a Karafka file, which BareArg would read as a topic when a literal follows; BareArg joins Receiver there. Test bare_arg_needs_a_word_edge (queue_topic.rs: `my_topic :orders` and `subtopic "orders"` -> no hit; `topic :orders` -> orders).

packets.rationale: Eight PHP messaging cells at HEAD 84e2e71: php/amqp = partial via=queue extract 2/2 literal 1/2 route 0/1 forbid 0/0 reason literal lost; php/kafka = partial via=queue extract 2/2 literal 1/2 route 0/1 forbid 0/0 reason literal lost; php/mqtt = none via=None extract 0/2 literal 0/2 route 0/1 forbid 0/0; php/nats = none via=None extract 0/2 literal 0/2 route 0/1 forbid 0/0; php/pubsub = none via=None extract 0/2 literal 0/2 route 0/1 forbid 0/0; php/redis = none via=None extract 0/2 literal 0/2 route 0/1 forbid 0/0; php/sqs_sns = none via=None extract 0/2 literal 0/2 route 0/1 forbid 0/0; php/taskq = none via=None extract 0/2 literal 0/2 route 0/1 forbid 0/0. Root cause shared by six: PHP calls methods with `->`, and every receiver-agnostic row in queues.rs is a leading-dot needle (`.publish(`, `.subscribe(`, `.topic(`, `.sendMessage(`), so no PHP client call matches. Measured per cell (GLIA_QUEUE_DEBUG=1): php/amqp - `basic_consume('orders', ..)` fires; php-amqplib's producer `$channel->basic_publish($msg, '', 'orders')` (github.com/php-amqplib/php-amqplib, positional `($msg, $exchange, $routing_key)`) is read only by the pika `basic_publish(` Keyed row (gate `amqp` passes on `PhpAmqpLib`), which finds no `routing_key=` and mints `queue_producer:unresolved:rabbitmq`. php/kafka - `newTopic("orders")` fires; php-rdkafka's `$consumer->subscribe(['orders'])` (arnaud-lb/php-rdkafka docs) has no row and the dotless `KafkaConsumer` row reads `$conf` from `new RdKafka\KafkaConsumer($conf)`, minting `queue_consumer:unresolved:kafka`. php/mqtt (php-mqtt/client `$mqtt->publish('sensors/temp', ..)` / `->subscribe(..)`), php/nats (basis-company/nats `$client->publish('orders', ..)` / `->subscribe(..)`), php/pubsub (googleapis/google-cloud-php `$pubsub->topic('orders')->publish(..)` / `->subscription('orders')`), php/sqs_sns (aws-sdk-php `$sqs->sendMessage(['QueueUrl' => ..])`) - nothing at all. php/redis - Laravel's facade `Redis::publish('orders', ..)` / `Redis::subscribe(['orders'], ..)` (laravel.com/docs/redis#pubsub) has no row (only the data_sources CACHE node fires). php/taskq - Laravel queued jobs (laravel.com/docs/queues: `class SendWelcomeEmail implements ShouldQueue` + `SendWelcomeEmail::dispatch()`) have no QueueFramework at all. The job class name is the join key (the Sidekiq / Oban A2.5 precedent): the worker runs the class's `handle()`, the dispatch site names the class.

packets.implementation:
1. GENERIC VERBS: add the three `->` spellings to GENERIC_VERB_NEEDLES; is_generic_verb_row stays framework-keyed (RedisPubSub | Mqtt), so the rdkafka / NATS `->subscribe(` rows read normally while the Redis / MQTT `->` rows need a leading literal and yield. Table order: the specific rows (rdkafka, NATS, SNS) precede the A2.9 block, so a phpredis call in a file that also imports basis/nats is attributed to NATS (the A2.9 claimed-span rule). 2. AMQP: `->basic_publish(` with ArgIndexOr(2, 1) - php-amqplib's routing key is positional arg #2; an empty key (`''`, fanout) falls back to the exchange (arg #1), amqplib's CL.1 rule. The HEAD pika `basic_publish(` row hits the same call (substring) and reads nothing; CL.1 rule (i) (overlapping span, same framework, named) suppresses its tag, so the file mints exactly `queue_producer:orders`. 3. RDKAFKA: `->subscribe(['orders'])` -> arg_literal reads the first literal inside the array. The HEAD `KafkaConsumer` row still hits `KafkaConsumer($conf)` and records the expression `$conf`, so rule (ii) cannot explain its tag; the two NoIdentity liveness rows overlap that hit (rule (i) liveness -> Explained::Overlap(None)) and the tag goes. A `use RdKafka\KafkaConsumer;` + `new KafkaConsumer($conf)` file is covered by the `new KafkaConsumer(` row. 4. SQS: aws-sdk-php takes an associative array; keyed_literal already reads `'QueueUrl' => '...'` (closing quote of the key, then `=>`), and fold_topic reduces the URL to `orders`. 5. LARAVEL JOBS: consumer = the job class (`ShouldQueue` needle, EnclosingSymbol reads the class on the needle's own line); producer = `X::dispatch(..)` (Receiver reads `X`) and the `dispatch(new X(..))` helper / `$this->dispatch(new X)` (ArgReceiver reads `X` through `new`). The `\jobs\` gate admits a file that imports a job; `laravel_job` then keeps a hit only for a class bound to a `Jobs` namespace (the `artisan make:job` home) or declared in the file as a ShouldQueue class, so `OrderPlaced::dispatch()` with `use App\Events\OrderPlaced;` (a Laravel EVENT, DH.7's) mints nothing here. An `X::dispatch()` hit of the helper row reads no argument; its deferred tag overlaps the `::dispatch(` hit that named X (rule (i)), so no tag. 6. TESTS (queues.rs mod tests): php_amqplib_positional_routing_key (matrix/php/amqp publisher.php -> exactly [queue_producer:orders]); php_amqplib_fanout_reads_exchange (`basic_publish($m, 'logs', '')` -> logs); php_rdkafka_subscribe_array_drops_the_consumer_tag (consumer.php -> exactly [queue_consumer:orders]); php_mqtt_client_publish_subscribe; php_basis_nats_publish_subscribe; php_gcp_pubsub_topic_subscription; php_laravel_redis_facade_and_phpredis (`Redis::publish('orders', ..)`, `Redis::subscribe(['orders'], ..)`, `$redis->publish('orders', $m)`); php_arrow_verb_needs_a_leading_literal (`$redis->publish($ch, $m)` -> no topic node); php_aws_sqs_array_keys_fold (-> orders, `from=url`); php_aws_sns_topic_arn; laravel_job_dispatch_pairs_should_queue (the two php/taskq files -> [queue_producer:SendWelcomeEmail] and [queue_consumer:SendWelcomeEmail]); laravel_helper_dispatch_new (`dispatch(new SendWelcomeEmail($u))`); laravel_event_dispatch_is_not_a_job (`use App\Events\OrderPlaced; OrderPlaced::dispatch(1);` -> nothing); laravel_shouldqueue_import_line_is_no_site (`use Illuminate\Contracts\Queue\ShouldQueue;` alone -> nothing, no tag); php_use_target_forms (plain, alias, group). 7. TABLE INVARIANT (verifier): queues.rs's mqtt_generic_guard_spares_builder_rows asserts that every RedisPubSub / Mqtt row outside three ad-hoc exemptions (`Mqtt` in the needle, a `*Async(` needle, `.WithTopicFilter(`) is a GENERIC_VERB_NEEDLES needle, so `Redis::publish(` / `Redis::subscribe(` / `Redis::psubscribe(` fail it. This commit restates that clause structurally: a RedisPubSub / Mqtt needle whose text after a leading `.` or `->` is a bare verb (`publish(` / `subscribe(` / `psubscribe(`, any ASCII case) must be a generic-verb row; every other RedisPubSub / Mqtt needle is a library row and exempt (the HEAD MQTTnet rows, these Laravel facade rows, DH.3's `.publishMessage(` / `.send_object(`, DH.4's Tortoise / Redix rows). The `->` verbs this packet adds to GENERIC_VERB_NEEDLES satisfy it; the test's first assertion (is_generic_verb_row == verb && pubsub) is unchanged. every_framework_tag_is_a_framework_tag's exhaustive list gains Laravel.
INTEGRATOR (0.5.2 merge, DF.2 cross-group): DF.2 (a dependency) binds a PHP `use` of a repo-declared namespace to that namespace's member and refuses the repo-unique tail guess; this packet's php fixtures are graded on top of it.

packets.risks: `->publish(` / `->subscribe(` / `->topic(` are common PHP method names: every row is gated on its package namespace (lowercased, `\\` in the Rust literal); the Redis / MQTT `->` rows are generic verbs (literal must lead). `dispatch(` is very broad (Redux, Symfony Messenger `$bus->dispatch(new X)`): the `\jobs\` gate plus `laravel_job` keep only Laravel job classes; a Messenger message class living under a `Jobs` namespace would read as a Laravel job (documented KNOWN IMPRECISION in the row comment). eventbus.rs's broker gate derives from these signals, so `publish(` / `.subscribe(` EVENT rows are skipped in files importing these clients (intended, A2.9). Byte offsets only; php_use_target scans lines and never slices mid-char. Same-file chain with DH.1 / DH.3 / DH.4 and DG queue packets. PARSER_STAMP moves. KNOWN IMPRECISION (verifier): Laravel queued listeners, mailables and notifications also implement ShouldQueue, so `class SendReceipt implements ShouldQueue` reads as a job consumer `queue_consumer:SendReceipt`; they do run on the queue worker, and no `::dispatch(` names them, so they stay unpaired consumer nodes (row comment).

Measured (GLIA_QUEUE_DEBUG=1, copies): dart/kafka - the consumer fires through the HEAD `consumer.subscribe` row, the kafka_dart producer `producer.sendMessage(topic: 'orders', ..)` (pub.dev/packages/kafka_dart README, verified 2026-10-02) is read by the `producer.send` KeyedOrArg row as a prefix, finds no bracket and mints `queue_producer:unresolved:kafka` (the 'literal lost'). dart/mqtt and dart/redis - the consumer fires through the generic `.subscribe(` rows; mqtt_client's producer `client.publishMessage(topic, qos, payload)` and package:redis's `cmd.send_object(['PUBLISH', 'orders', ..])` (its README's pub/sub example) have no row. dart/amqp - dart_amqp (pub.dev/packages/dart_amqp) binds the queue by DECLARATION: `final queue = await channel.queue('orders');` then `queue.consume()` / `queue.publish('order-1')` - neither call names the queue, and CL.1's declare pass runs on the consumer side only. dart/nats (dart_nats `client.sub('orders')` / `client.pubString('orders', ..)`), dart/pubsub (googleapis pubsub/v1 `api.projects.topics.publish(req, 'projects/shop/topics/orders')` / `api.projects.subscriptions.pull(req, 'projects/shop/subscriptions/orders')`), dart/sqs_sns (aws_sqs_api `sqs.sendMessage(queueUrl: ..)`: the `.sendMessage(` row's gate lists no Dart package) and dart/taskq (redis_task_queue `client.enqueue(Task('email:welcome', ..))` / `worker.handle('email:welcome', ..)`, pub.dev README verified 2026-10-02) mint nothing.

packets.implementation: 1. DECLARATIONS ON BOTH SIDES: CL.1's bind_declared_queues is side-agnostic (it binds every unnamed hit of a declared framework to the file's one declared queue); only the table differed. PRODUCER_DECLARE_PATTERNS feeds the producer emit, so dart_amqp's `channel.queue('orders')` + `queue.publish('order-1')` mints `queue_producer:orders` at the publish offset, exactly as `queue.consume()` mints the consumer. The publish row is `Declared` (DH.1's rule): dart_amqp's `Queue.publish(message)` argument is the PAYLOAD, which ArgLiteral would read as the topic. KNOWN IMPRECISION (row comment): an `exchange.publish(msg, key)` in a file that also declares exactly one queue binds to that queue. 2. COMMANDARG (queue_topic.rs): `command_arg(region, cmd)` walks the region's quoted literals in order (split_args over the list's elements, nesting respected); on the first literal equal to `cmd` ignoring ASCII case, it returns fold_topic of the NEXT literal; else None. No expression slot. Used for `.send_object(['PUBLISH', 'orders', ..])` here and DH.4's Redix. 3. KAFKA_DART: the `.sendMessage(` row names the topic; the HEAD `producer.send` row's hit on the same call (its needle is a prefix of `producer.sendMessage(`) reads nothing, and CL.1 rule (i) (overlap, same framework, named) suppresses its tag. 4. NATS / PUBSUB / SQS / TASKQ rows as listed. googleapis passes the full resource name, which fold_topic reduces (`projects/shop/topics/orders` -> orders, the A2.6 GCP rule). A subscription pairs only when spelled like its topic (the declared COVERAGE_CAVEATS gap, unchanged). redis_task_queue's `client.enqueue(Task('email:welcome', ..))`: arg #0 is the Task constructor, whose first literal is the task type. 5. packets.implementation: 1. KEYEDIN (queue_topic.rs): `enclosing_region(source, offset)` walks BACK from the needle over at most MAX_REGION bytes, skipping quoted text, to the nearest unmatched `{` / `[` / `(`, then forward to its match (balanced, quotes skipped, MAX_REGION bound); `keyed_in(region, keys)` = keyed_literal's key search (word edges, `:` / `=>` / `=` separators), but at the value it steps over up to two opening `[` / `{` (and whitespace) before read_literal. topic_at: `KeyedIn(keys) => keyed_in(arg_region(..).or_else(|| enclosing_region(..))?, keys)`; expr_at returns None for it (an option value that is a variable names nothing). Elixir keywords (`topics: [..]`, `subscription: ".."`), maps (`%{topic: ".."}`) and the Tortoise subscription tuple (`[{"sensors/temp", 0}]`) all read. 2. OBAN PIPE (queue_topic.rs arg_receiver): unchanged when arg #0 exists (`Oban.insert(EmailWorker.new(%{}))`); else `piped_receiver(source, offset)`: trailing whitespace before the needle, then `|>`, then the previous stage back to the prior `|>` or the line start; the stage must be `<Chain>.new(` + a balanced argument list ending the stage -> last segment of Chain. `Oban.insert!` / `Oban.insert_all` go through the same needle (`Oban.insert` prefix) and the same fallback. 3. ROWS as listed. Gates are each library's lowercased module token, so they also feed eventbus.rs's derived broker gate: an Elixir file using Redix / Gnat / Tortoise skips the generic `.subscribe(` EVENT row (A2.9's intent; today such a call can mint a Weak EVENT_HANDLER). brod's subscriber topics arg is a list: ArgIndex reads its first literal. 4. TESTS (queues.rs): elixir_amqp_consume_reads_queue (matrix/elixir/amqp worker.ex -> [queue_consumer:orders]); broadway_kafka_topics_list_multiline (the hexdocs producer config spread over five lines -> orders); brod_produce_sync_and_group_subscriber; tortoise311_publish_and_subscriptions; gnat_pub_sub_and_consumer_supervisor (`subscription_topics: [%{topic: "rpc.example"}]` -> rpc.example); broadway_cloud_pubsub_subscription_folds; google_api_pubsub_topics_publish; redix_publish_command_and_pubsub_subscribe (`["GET", "k"]` -> no node, no tag); ex_aws_sqs_send_and_receive; oban_pipe_insert_reads_the_worker (matrix/elixir/taskq signup.ex -> exactly [queue_producer:MailerWorker], no tag); oban_insert_argument_form_unchanged. queue_topic.rs: keyed_in_reads_the_enclosing_tuple; keyed_in_steps_into_a_list_of_tuples; keyed_in_variable_value_reads_nothing; arg_receiver_reads_the_pipe_stage; arg_receiver_pipe_needs_a_new_stage (`|> Repo.insert()` -> None). 5. GATE PRECISION (verifier): every broker gate in these tables feeds eventbus.rs's derived broker gate (broker_signal_present) for EVERY language, and a file that passes it loses its in-process `.on(` / `.subscribe(` / `publish(` EVENT nodes. The bare word `gnat` is a substring of `signature` and `designated`, so it would silence those EVENT rows in any TS / Python / Go file that mentions a signature; the Gnat rows are gated on GNAT (Gnat's call spellings) instead. Tortoise / Redix / BroadwayKafka / BroadwayCloudPubSub / GoogleApi.PubSub / ExAws.SQS / `:brod` gates are library tokens no common word contains. Test broker_gate_ignores_signature_text (queues.rs): broker_signal_present("const signature = sign(payload)") is false, and an eventbus.rs test file `emitter.on('saved', h)` beside `signature` still mints its EVENT_HANDLER. 6. INVARIANT: the Tortoise (Mqtt) and Redix (RedisPubSub) rows are library rows, exempt under DH.2's restated mqtt_generic_guard_spares_builder_rows.

packets.title: Ruby type and call facts: `class X < Base` INHERITS_FROM, dry-auto_inject `include Import["key"]` INJECTS (fixture rewritten to the real dry-rb API), and `Calc.new.add(..)` binding through the constructed type so Minitest methods get function-level TESTS

packets.rationale: At HEAD 84e2e71: ruby/impl = partial via=type extract 1/1 literal 1/1 route 0/1 forbid 0/0 reason routing edge missing; ruby/injects = partial via=di extract 2/2 literal 2/2 route 0/1 forbid 0/0 reason routing edge missing; ruby/tests = partial via=test extract 2/2 literal 2/2 route 1/2 forbid 0/0 reason routing edge missing. ruby/impl: `class UserRepository < BaseRepository` emits no INHERITS_FROM (debug CLI: only IMPORTS user_repository -> base_repository): parsers/code/ruby reads the `superclass` field only inside emit_ar_model_entity (the ActiveRecord check), never as a heritage ref, while build_ruby already runs resolve_refs, whose Bare INHERITS_FROM path binds module symbols then a repo-unique name (the Dart A6.5 shape). ruby/injects (classified FIXTURE-WRONG, then fixable): the fixture requires dry/container but never uses it - `def initialize(user_service)` is an untyped parameter that names no type, so no DI fact exists in the source; a name-guess from `user_service` to `UserService` would be a heuristic with no library behind it. The real dry-rb idiom is dry-auto_inject (dry-rb.org/gems/dry-auto_inject): `Import = Dry::AutoInject(Container)` + `include Import["user_service"]`, the container registering `register("user_service") { UserService.new }`; dry-system's auto-registration derives a key from the component's file / class name with Dry::Inflector, so a key's last segment camelised IS the library's own name rule. The fixture is rewritten to that API (same classes, same expected INJECTS OrderController -> UserService). ruby/tests: the module pairing fires (`TESTS calc_test -> calc`); the function-level edge needs a CALLS edge from CalcTest#test_adds to Calc#add for CL.5b, but collect_call drops a call whose receiver is itself a call (`Calc.new.add(2, 3)`: receiver `Calc.new` is a `call` node), and CL.5a's constructed_type reads only the prefix `new X(..)` form.

HERITAGE: the ref goes through build_ruby's resolve_refs; a framework base (`ActiveRecord::Base`, `Minitest::Test`) binds nothing and emits nothing; `ApplicationRecord` binds to the app's own class (correct). The AR model check keeps reading the same field. 2. AUTO_INJECT: the argument of `include` must be an element_reference whose object is a constant (optionally `.args` / `.hash` / `.kwargs`), and its elements string / symbol literals - Ruby's `include` takes a Module, and `Const[..]` returning one is the auto_inject builder, so no other library matches the shape. Camelise: split `_`, capitalise each part (`user_service` -> `UserService`); dotted keys use their last segment (`repositories.users` -> `Users`). The ref is an INJECTS Bare(type) from the class, resolved by resolve_refs' INJECTS global-unique fallback (the TS / Java Pattern E path), EVIDENCE `graph:refs` with that branch's rule. 3. CONSTRUCTED RECEIVER: collect_call's receiver branch adds the `call`-node case above; graph's constructed_type gains the postfix form after its prefix-`new` branch (`text.strip_suffix(")")` balanced back to `.new(`, or `text.ends_with(".new")`), then the same constructed_type_id lookup (import binding -> module symbol -> unique global type). CL.5b then mints `TESTS CalcTest::test_adds -> Calc::add` from the new CALLS edge (no change to passes.rs). 4. packets.title: Elixir remote calls by full module name: `Shop.Cart.total(..)` and an un-aliased top-level `Cart.total(..)` bind to the module's function (today only an `alias`-ed short name binds)
packets.area: DH matrix elixir tests prerequisite (elixir/tests; Elixir CALLS in general)
packets.rationale: Measured at HEAD 84e2e71 with the debug CLI on a two-file probe under the spec probe dir (lib/cart.ex `defmodule Shop.Cart do def total(xs) ..`, lib/caller.ex calling it three ways): `alias Shop.Cart` + `Cart.total([1, 2])` -> CALLS go -> Shop.Cart::total (bound through the alias import binding); `Shop.Cart.total([3])` -> NO edge; and with a top-level `defmodule Cart`, an un-aliased `Cart.total(..)` -> NO edge (the same holds in matrix/elixir/tests' cart_test.exs). Cause: the Elixir parser emits a remote call as CallQualifier::Attribute { base: "Shop.Cart", name: "total" }, and resolve_attribute_target binds an Attribute base only through the module's import bindings; Elixir module names are global atoms, so the fully-qualified form needs no alias and is the common style in contexts, tests and pipelines. build_dotted (shared with Java, Kotlin, C#, PHP, Scala, Clojure) passes `|_, _| None` as resolve_calls' extra_hook, so nothing tries the module's own name. elixir/calls reads full only because its fixture holds an intra-module call; ExUnit tests (DH.17b) call the module under test by its name, so elixir/tests cannot reach CL.5b without this.

packets.rationale: At HEAD 84e2e71: elixir/impl = none via=None extract 0/1 literal 0/1 route 0/1 forbid 0/0; elixir/injects = none via=None extract 0/1 literal 0/1 route 0/1 forbid 0/0; elixir/tests = partial via=test extract 1/1 literal 1/1 route 1/2 forbid 0/0 reason routing edge missing. elixir/impl: `defmodule Shop.Notifier do @callback notify(String.t()) :: :ok end` is a behaviour (hexdocs.pm/elixir/typespecs.html#behaviours), the contract `@behaviour Shop.Notifier` implementations declare; the parser emits every defmodule as a PACKAGE (visit_defmodule) and reads no `@behaviour`, so there is neither an INTERFACE nor an IMPLEMENTS edge. `defprotocol` is already an INTERFACE (visit_defprotocol), so a behaviour taking the same kind is the parser's own precedent. elixir/injects: Elixir's DI idiom is a module attribute read from config with a default implementation, `@repo Application.compile_env(:shop, :user_repo, Shop.PgUserRepo)` (the Mox 'explicit contracts' pattern, hexdocs.pm/mox; Application.compile_env/3 docs). The default module IS named in the source; the parser reads no module attribute. elixir/tests: ExUnit's `test "sums" do .. end` (hexdocs.pm/ex_unit/ExUnit.Case.html#test/3) defines the function `:"test sums"`, but the parser emits no node for it and collects no calls from its body, so CL.5b has no test function and no CALLS to read; only the module pairing `cart_test -> cart` exists. Today the grader's substring match would accept PgUserRepo for `UserRepo` by accident, so the row is made exact (`PgUserRepo`) and the IMPLEMENTS hop is asserted under the impl mechanism.

Refs resolve in build_dotted's resolve_refs: IMPLEMENTS / INJECTS Bare names go module symbols -> repo-unique name (Elixir module nodes are named by their last segment, visit_defmodule's `short`), so `Shop.Notifier` binds the unique `Notifier` module; two modules named `Notifier` in different namespaces stay unresolved. emit_method_level_implements pairs `notify/1` implementations with the callback when the behaviour declares it as a FUNCTION-kind member - callbacks are typespecs, not defs, so no method-level edge is expected (documented). 3. compile_env: only the 3-argument form with a module-alias default (capitalised dotted atom) names a target; `Application.get_env(:shop, :user_repo)` without a default names nothing and emits nothing. 4. packets.title: Clojure route handlers: Compojure `(GET "/p" [args] (handler ..))` / `(GET "/p" [] handler)` and reitit `["/p" {:get handler}]` / `{:get {:handler h}}` -> HANDLED_BY
packets.rationale: At HEAD 84e2e71: clojure/http_server = partial via=http extract 1/1 literal 1/1 route 2/4 forbid 1/1 reason routing edge missing. Routes, methods and both HTTP_CALLS pairings are found; scan_clojure_routes (parsers/code/clojure/src/lib.rs) takes no module id and emits no HANDLED_BY, so the route never reaches its handler function. In Compojure (github.com/weavejester/compojure/wiki/Routes-In-Detail) the form after the argument binding is the response body - idiomatically a call of the handler `(get-user id)` or a bare handler var; in reitit (cljdoc.org/d/metosin/reitit) a method key maps to a handler fn or to `{:handler f}`.
entry_points: parsers/code/clojure/src/lib.rs - scan_clojure_routes - takes module_id (parse_file passes it); Compojure: after the path literal, skip the binding form (a vector `[..]`, a map `{..}` or a symbol) and read the body form: `(f ..)` with a symbol head -> Bare(f) (`ns/f` -> Attribute { base: ns, name: f }); a bare symbol -> Bare(sym); reitit: in the route-data map, `:<method> <symbol>` and `:<method> {.. :handler <symbol> ..}` -> the same refs

packets.title: C / C++ HTTP clients through libcurl's easy interface: `curl_easy_setopt(h, CURLOPT_URL, "..")` mints an ENDPOINT whose verb comes from the same handle's options (POSTFIELDS / POST / CUSTOMREQUEST / UPLOAD / NOBODY)
packets.rationale: At HEAD 84e2e71: c_cpp/http_client = none via=None extract 0/2 literal 0/2 route 0/2 forbid 1/1. Debug CLI on a copy: the Go chi server's ROUTEs exist; the C client mints no ENDPOINT - parsers/code/c_cpp has no HTTP client reading at all. libcurl's easy interface is the dominant C HTTP client (curl.se/libcurl/c/curl_easy_setopt.html): the URL is set with `CURLOPT_URL`, the request is GET unless an option on the SAME handle changes it - `CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS` / `CURLOPT_COPYPOSTFIELDS` / `CURLOPT_POST` / `CURLOPT_MIMEPOST` make it POST, `CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST, "PUT"` names the verb, `CURLOPT_UPLOAD` is PUT, `CURLOPT_NOBODY` is HEAD. The fixture's forbid (create_user must not reach GET /users) is exactly that same-handle rule.
entry_points: parsers/code/c_cpp/src/lib.rs - visit_callable - after collect_body_facts: (new) collect_curl_endpoints(body, src, fn_id, acc)

parsers/code/c_cpp/src/lib.rs - (new) collect_curl_endpoints - walk the body's call_expression nodes whose function is the identifier `curl_easy_setopt`: group by the handle argument's text; per handle keep the CURLOPT_URL string literal(s) and the method options; then one ClientEndpoint per (handle, URL): method = CUSTOMREQUEST literal (upper-cased) > NOBODY HEAD > UPLOAD PUT > POSTFIELDS / COPYPOSTFIELDS / POST / MIMEPOST POST > GET; path = glia_code_domain::endpoint::normalise_client_path(url) (scheme + host + query dropped); pushed through endpoint::push_client_endpoint from fn_id, Confidence Medium, file = the file's path, line / col = the CURLOPT_URL call's
parsers/code/c_cpp/src/lib.rs - Acc - gains `file_rel: String` (set in Acc::new from parse_tree_into's file path) and `endpoint_hits: usize` + a seen-set for push_client_endpoint
parsers/code/c_cpp/src/lib.rs - parse_file - per-file marker `[c-http-client] endpoints=<n> (libcurl=<n>) path=<file>` when n > 0 (the `[ruby-http-client]` / `[elixir-http-client]` lines' shape)
packets.implementation: 1. Same-handle grouping is per function body: a handle created and configured in one function (the canonical shape) gets every option; a URL set on a handle whose options live in another function reads as GET (documented). A non-literal URL (`url` variable, `snprintf` buffer) names nothing - no ENDPOINT, no `<unresolved>` node. 2. Verb literal: `CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST, "DELETE"` -> DELETE; a non-literal custom request keeps the option-derived default. `CURLOPT_HTTPGET` resets to GET. 3. HttpStackResolver pairs `endpoint:GET:/users` with the chi ROUTE `GET /users` through the existing method + path rules; the ENDPOINT_HIT cell carries `"method":"POST"` and the file, as the other clients' do. 4. TESTS (c_cpp parser mod tests): libcurl_default_get (matrix/c_cpp/http_client list_users -> endpoint GET /users, CALLS from list_users); libcurl_postfields_is_post (create_user -> POST /users, and NO GET /users from create_user); libcurl_customrequest_verb; libcurl_upload_put_and_nobody_head; libcurl_two_handles_in_one_function; libcurl_variable_url_names_nothing; cpp_member_function_client (the same calls inside a C++ method -> CALLS from the METHOD). 5. PRECEDENT (verifier): the PHP parser already reads ext-curl the same way (parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs: `curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_URL, '..')`, an explicit CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST literal wins, then CURLOPT_POST*, else GET, over the whole body); this packet's per-handle grouping is the C refinement the fixture's forbid (create_user must not reach GET /users) needs, and its option precedence matches that reader's.

RULE: every break, name, marker and number comes from the LANDED commits (each packet's commit body and its `breaking` result in closeout's per-wave summary), checked against the code; this packet's rationale is the checklist, not the source. Each handoff opens with the exact pin (glia-py==0.5.2 on PyPI after James publishes; crates `=0.5.2` path / tag v0.5.2), a TL;DR of what the consumer must change versus what is optional, then the sections in entry_points. The repo-graph WatchSession section gives the seven steps with file / function names verified against /home/ivy/Code/repo-graph (read-only: repo_graph/server.py _watch_rebuild / _build_graph / _release_freed_memory, repo_graph/watcher.py Debouncer / _Handler) and quotes DC.9's RSS rows for the snapshot cadence. The neuropil handoff lists every pub API signature change from the api_signature breaks and runs neuropil's compile check against the release commit (read-only, CARGO_TARGET_DIR under /home/ivy/.cache, rm -rf after) - or states it was not run and why. The Engram handoff re-measures nothing itself: it cites DE.2's determinism gate output, DE.3 / DE.4's Kina chain numbers and DE.5's side-file format from their commit bodies, and lists DE's open questions (DE.4's precision-over-recall trade, DE.5's format) as 'Engram to confirm'. GAP PACKETS ADDED AFTER INTEGRATION (DB.9a-c, Q9 rules through the overlay loop; DF.22a-c, TS typed-receiver inherited calls + concrete-override dispatch): their doc lines, routed here:
- DZ.1 correction: drop skills/glia-overlay/SKILL.md "`overlay try` measures no rule stanza (the Q9 gap, open)". DB.9a-c close that gap; the lines below replace it
- skills/glia-overlay/SKILL.md `## The candidate file` / Sections: a candidate may also hold [[constraint]] rules: forbid_edge (incl. transitive / via), no_cycle, and invariant with `rule`, with min_tier per DB.1 (fact | derived). `kind = "allow"` and prose (text-only) invariants are refused. Each rule needs a fresh id. `version` is optional: accept raises the file to `version = 2` in place only when a written rule uses rule / transitive / via / min_tier, and refuses the raise when it would also load a stanza version 1 drops
- skills/glia-overlay/SKILL.md `## What to write, per suggest`: glia drafts no rule. Write one only from declared intent: a prose invariant `glia check` lists unchecked, an ADR or [[decision]], or the person's request. Use structural predicates only (SECURITY.md); docs/rules.md documents `rule` text
- skills/glia-overlay/SKILL.md `## Reading the try report`: a [[constraint]] stanza shows its `rule` status (holds / violated / error / orphaned / duplicate) and any `empty_scopes`. holds = keep; holds with an empty scope, or violated = review; error / orphaned / duplicate = drop. A graph stanza that adds or hides a declared rule's violation is review. The verdict line has a graph part and a rule part. Also the `rules` column, the rules block, the `rules:` totals line and the `[overlay] try-rules` marker
- skills/glia-overlay/SKILL.md `## Accepting and pruning`: handles are `constraint#<n>`. An identical rule counts as a duplicate. A same-id rule with another body is refused (exit 1): edit the file by hand or pick another id. A rule whose text does not validate, or that defines no `violation`, is refused (exit 1); try reports it as error -> drop
- skills/glia-overlay/SKILL.md `## Cost`: try runs at most 2 + (number of graph stanzas) builds, because rule stanzas are judged on the WITH build. Each build that carries a rule also runs glia check (`[check]` lines per build)
- CLAUDE.md Query & Answer Surface, inputs bullet `overlay propose|try|accept` (CE.3e): it also takes [[constraint]] rules (DB.9a-c, Q9). try judges a rule by the check delta and demotes a graph stanza that moves a declared rule's violation. accept refuses a rule check cannot evaluate. pyo3 overlay_try returns `rules` and each stanza's `rule` / `rules`; engine overlay_loop exports RuleHit / RulesDelta / RuleTrial / RulesReport
- README.md, the `overlay propose / try / accept` prose and the 0.5.2 notes: rules an agent proposes go through the overlay loop and are judged by the violations they find on the code as it is
- py/README.md (overlay_try line): the dict gains `rules` when a build checked a rule or the candidate holds a [[constraint]]. Stanza dicts gain `rule` / `rules`. overlay_accept raises ValueError on a rule check cannot evaluate
- dev-notes/repo-graph-handoff-0.5.2.md: the `[overlay] candidate` / `[overlay] accept` markers gain ` constraint=<n>`, and there is a new `[overlay] try-rules` line. overlay_try's dict gains optional `rules` and per-stanza `rule` / `rules`. Graph-stanza verdicts change when a stanza moves a declared rule's violation. [[constraint]] candidates are now accepted, and one whose rule does not validate is refused. The wrapper calls no overlay_* today (grep: 0 hits)
- README.md ## Roadmap 'Next: 0.5.2': drop 'In TypeScript: typed-receiver inherited calls, concrete-override dispatch' (shipped by DF.22a-c)
- README.md, the TypeScript language section and the 0.5.2 changes: (1) TS parameters and locals now type their receivers: annotated, `new T()`, `inject(T)`, `x as T`, and `this.<field>` aliases. Locals in top-level test callbacks (describe / it) share the file's scope (DF.22a, `[ts-locals]`). (2) A typed-receiver call into an inherited method binds the nearest superclass method (DF.22b, EVIDENCE rule inherited_receiver, `[ts-inherit] .. receiver=`). (3) A concrete override IMPLEMENTS the member it overrides (DF.22c, rule concrete_override, `concrete overrides=`), so liveness and dead_symbol dispatch to it. (4) `super.m()` is rule super_method and vouches for no override in dead_symbol. (5) `glia coverage` on a TS repo lists a typescript CALLS row
- CLAUDE.md, Parser-vs-Graph Split, TS bullet: `resolve_inherited_calls` binds `this.m()` (rule `inherited_method`), `super.m()` (rule `super_method`, DF.22c) and typed-receiver calls whose class inherits m (rule `inherited_receiver`, DF.22b). `emit_override_implements` (renamed from emit_abstract_implements) pairs an override with the member it overrides: abstract (`NavFact::AbstractMethod`, rule `abstract_override`, CH.1b) or concrete (rule `concrete_override`, DF.22c). Constructors never pair (`[ts-inherit]`). The TS parser fills CodeNav::local_types for parameters and locals (DF.22a, `[ts-locals]`)
- CLAUDE.md, Query & Answer Surface, inputs / gaps: append to the dead_symbol sentence that a `super.m()` call (rule super_method) vouches for nothing, and that TS concrete overrides join the dispatch rule through rule concrete_override (DF.22c)
- dev-notes/repo-graph-handoff-0.5.2.md, neuropil-handoff-0.5.2.md, engram-handoff-0.5.2.md. Additive: more TS CALLS (rule receiver_type) from parameter and local receivers, including module-scope test callbacks (DF.22a); CALLS rule inherited_receiver (DF.22b); method-level IMPLEMENTS rule concrete_override (DF.22c), which Engram receives as Implements facts between existing method Symbols. Breaking (cell_value): a TS `super.m()` CALLS edge's EVIDENCE rule changes from inherited_method to super_method. Changed output: `[ts-inherit]` reads `(self= super= receiver= ambiguous=) abstract implements= concrete overrides=`; new `[ts-locals]` stderr line; dead_symbol rows change (a method that gains its first caller leaves; TS overrides of a called member are withheld; overridden concrete members leave the list); `glia coverage` gains a TS CALLS row; patterns / check / reflexion counts read the new edges. No qname or identity_hint moves

DF.22c reverses CH.1b's stance that 'a concrete override is not IMPLEMENTS'. That stance was the CH.1b author's design note, not a recorded ruling by James (no ruling found in next-leap-0.5.1.md, leap-051-corrections.json or the 0.5.2 plan). The spec models dispatch as the method-level IMPLEMENTS hop (A6.6 / CA.3b / CH.1b); every consumer already follows it, and CE.1e's SCIP import maps METHOD -> METHOD is_implementation to IMPLEMENTS. The alternative is a method-level INHERITS_FROM plus a new hop in live_walk, gaps and tests_for. James decides before DF.22c's wave (W11)

Liveness stays node-level generous. IMPLEMENTS is a forward carry edge, so a reached override makes the member it overrides live, and the implementer step then makes every sibling override live, as interface and abstract pairs already do. A base reached only through an override's `super.m()` does the same. DF.22c makes only dead_symbol's dispatch rule exact for super calls; an edge-aware liveness is not specced

dead_symbol's dispatch rule stays node-level, as CH.1c's is. A call on an exactly typed receiver (`new T().m()`, a `new` local) vouches for T's overrides, although none can run there. Example: mem0's openai-llm.test.ts `new OpenAILLM(..)` local vouches for the DeepSeekLLM / LMStudioLLM overrides. That is moot on mem0, since their own tests call them, but it is a general imprecision. Separating exact-type receivers would need their own EVIDENCE rule
